slot.brief: A lens of known glass placed in a liquid of given refractive index; find the new focal length or determine whether it acts as a converging or diverging lens.

stem: A thin converging lens of focal length $10\text{ cm}$ (refractive index $\mu_1 = 1.5$) and a thin diverging lens of focal length $20\text{ cm}$ (refractive index $\mu_2 = 1.6$) are placed in contact coaxially in air. When the combination is completely immersed in water of refractive index $\dfrac{4}{3}$, it behaves as a:
options: converging lens of focal length $80\text{ cm}$
diverging lens of focal length $80\text{ cm}$
converging lens of focal length $120\text{ cm}$
diverging lens of focal length $120\text{ cm}$
working:
Using the lens-maker formula in a medium of refractive index $\mu_{\text{m}}$:
$$\dfrac{f_{\text{m}}}{f_{\text{air}}} = \dfrac{\mu - 1}{\dfrac{\mu}{\mu_{\text{m}}} - 1}$$

For the converging lens ($\mu_1 = 1.5$, $f_{1,\text{air}} = +10\text{ cm}$):
$$\dfrac{f_{1,\text{w}}}{10} = \dfrac{1.5 - 1}{\dfrac{1.5}{4/3} - 1} = \dfrac{0.5}{\dfrac{9}{8} - 1} = \dfrac{0.5}{1/8} = 4$$
$$f_{1,\text{w}} = 4 \times (+10) = +40\text{ cm}$$

For the diverging lens ($\mu_2 = 1.6$, $f_{2,\text{air}} = -20\text{ cm}$):
$$\dfrac{f_{2,\text{w}}}{-20} = \dfrac{1.6 - 1}{\dfrac{1.6}{4/3} - 1} = \dfrac{0.6}{1.2 - 1} = \dfrac{0.6}{0.2} = 3$$
$$f_{2,\text{w}} = 3 \times (-20) = -60\text{ cm}$$

For the thin combination in water:
$$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{f_{1,\text{w}}} + \dfrac{1}{f_{2,\text{w}}} = \dfrac{1}{40} - \dfrac{1}{60} = \dfrac{3 - 2}{120} = +\dfrac{1}{120}\text{ cm}^{-1}$$
$$F = +120\text{ cm}$$

Since $F > 0$, the combination behaves as a converging lens of focal length $120\text{ cm}$.

Independent check: Lensmaker: P = (μ_rel − 1)K. In air: K1 = (1/10)/0.5 = 0.2 cm⁻¹, K2 = (−1/20)/0.6 = −1/12 cm⁻¹. In water: μ1/μw = 9/8 → P1 = (1/8)(0.2) = 1/40; μ2/μw = 6/5 → P2 = (1/5)(−1/12) = −1/60. Total P = 1/40 − 1/60 = 1/120 cm⁻¹ → f = +120 cm, converging.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option A comes from assuming both lenses scale by the rote factor of 4 (applicable only when $\mu = 1.5$), giving $F = 4 \times 20\text{ cm} = 80\text{ cm}$.
Option B combines the rote factor of 4 with a sign error regarding the resulting nature.
Option D comes from finding the correct magnitude ($120\text{ cm}$) but making a sign mistake in $\frac{1}{F} = \frac{1}{f_1} + \frac{1}{f_2}$, concluding it is diverging.
